question: Does fixed off-by-one attention, with an exact zero K/V option competing in each attention softmax, improve Japanese continuation under unchanged original CE and native parameter coordinates?
formula: For visible real logits z_j=q.k_j*original_scale: y=sum(exp(z_j)*v_j)/(1+sum(exp(z_j))). A fixed zero Key and zero Value, not a vocabulary token, not learned, not RoPE-shifted.
main_change: One fixed zero-logit zero-value alternative inside attention normalization; no new Q/K/V projections, no coefficient/output projection rescaling, no learned sink/gate or vocabulary/output distribution change.
rationale: A different missing-capability hypothesis from signed-map selection: attention can abstain on a query even when all real reads are unhelpful. Existing repeated-output failures motivate testing a distinct mechanism; no local proof that unwanted mixing causes them.

novelty.headwise_gate: Closed post-SDPA sigmoid(W*x) gate depends on current normalized query representation, doubles O and introduces new coordinates. Here unchanged O/coordinates; attenuation Z/(1+Z) depends jointly on all visible keys and query. Dense counterexample must show same query and native softmax map/output but different quiet output after shifting all real scores.
novelty.forgetting: No pairwise time-decay/logsigmoid gates, cumulative log history or mask bias. Fixed additional zero alternative has no learned parameters and preserves real relative probabilities.
novelty.sigsoftmax: Acts only within attention, not the normalized vocabulary distribution. Original output softmax and gold CE unchanged.
